reasons.claim: Consistent, price-dependent buybacks have returned meaningful capital, with a 4.5% repurchase yield over nine years.
reasons.quote: during the past nine years they repurchased nine percent of the shares outstanding so that is a four point five percent repurchase yield and he spent 51 billion for that

data_check.gap_note: he says 5.1e+10, as-of -2.4706e+10 (FY2020); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: shares repurchased, repurchase yield

reasons.claim: Berkshire has $114 billion in deployable cash beyond its safety buffer that could add materially to earnings once invested, though it has not yet found where to deploy it.
reasons.quote: if he could invest that with a 10 return that would add 11.4 billion dollars to berkshire's earnings but he has to find the way where to deploy that money that is something he didn't yet find over the last years

data_check.gap_note: he says 1.14e+11, as-of 4.8396e+10 (FY2020); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: If interest rates rise and investors demand better returns, the stock could fall back to prior lower price levels.
reasons.quote: if interest rates go higher and investors expect better returns then one should not be surprised to see the stock go back to the levels that it was there a few years ago

reasons.claim: Berkshire's diversification, fee-free structure, and quality management make it unlikely you will lose money long term, similar to an index fund.
reasons.quote: it's unlikely that you will lose money in the long term with berkshire especially if measured in u.s dollars so diversification so it's like owning an index fund no fees and very smart people and a great culture

external_facts_used: Buffett's 2021 shareholder letter disclosing $144 billion cash and $30 billion minimum cash reserve policy
Berkshire's ~5.6% ownership stake in Apple and Apple's ~$100 billion in earnings
Buybacks: 9% of shares repurchased over nine years for $51 billion, plus $1.2 billion repurchased through Feb 23, 2022
